text_en:
Zayd ibn Ali, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with them, said: "Call Hasan and Husayn for me." So I called them, and he began to kiss them until he fainted. He said: And Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, lifted them from his face, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said:

Imam al-Mansur Billah Abu Ali al-Hasan ibn Badr al-Din, may Allah be pleased with him, said in his book "Anwar al-Yaqin fi Fadail Amir al-Mu'minin Ali," may Allah be pleased with him, the following:

text_ar: 0 حدثي ( ز ىك نْ عي عن أدمه عن سيت ه عن عل ر ضي ابله عنه.م قال : وأبعنا رسول الله ا 34 و كنا تيأبعه على السمع والطاعة 2 المكره والتشط: ج 8 امقر والعسر 6 وف الاثرة عاينأ وأن لقم العقنا بالفدل ول هين فى الله لومة لاثم » فلم! كير الإسلام قال رسول الله ع لعلي ر ضي ألله عنك :زر لمق فيها وإن منعوا رسو ن” الله وذ 00 ما عسعوان مسنه أنفسكم وذراريكم 4) قال فوضعتها والله على رقاب القوم ذوفا ها من وفاا ء وهلأت بها من هلات .
text_en:
Zayd ibn Ali narrated from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) who said:

"We pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and we would follow him in hearing and obedience, in what we liked and disliked, in ease and hardship, and in being preferred over others. And that we would not dispute authority with its people, and that we would speak the truth wherever we were, and not fear the blame of any blamer for the sake of Allah."

When Islam became widespread, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said to Ali (may Allah be pleased with him): "Fight for it, even if they prevent you from the Messenger of Allah, and protect yourselves and your offspring."

Ali said: "By Allah, I placed it upon the necks of the people, fearing its consequences, and I averted calamities with it."

text_en: Ali ibn al-Husayn, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to me – and he was holding a hair – he said:

text_en: Zayd ibn Ali, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with them) said: A man said to him: "O Commander of the Believers, what do you think about the leftover water of camels, and a man walking in a single sandal, and a man drinking while standing?" He said: "He entered the courtyard. And it is from the Sunnah of drinking that one should not breathe into the vessel, as narrated by Al-Bukhari from the path of Abu Qatadah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'When one of you drinks, he should not breathe into the vessel.' Al-Khattabi said: 'His prohibition (peace be upon him) of breathing into the vessel is a prohibition of etiquette and instruction. This is because if he does that, he is not safe from saliva falling into it and mixing with the water, which would make the drinker dislike it. And sometimes it might acquire the odor of the breather if it was foul, because water, due to its subtlety and thinness, quickly absorbs odors. Furthermore, it is considered an act of animals when they drink from vessels, they gulp, then breathe into them, then return to drink. The Sunnah and etiquette are that one should drink water in three breaths, each time he drinks a breath from the vessel, he moves it away from his mouth, then returns to it, sipping without interruption.' And I saw him, and he had a bucket, and he scooped from its excess and drank while standing. And he wore one of his sandals until he came out of the courtyard. The man said: 'O Commander of the Believers, you have done what you forbade me from doing!' He said: 'What did I do?'"

text_en: The Commander of the Believers, Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to me, while he was holding a hair, he said:

text_ar: حدثني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وهى أخذه بشعرة قال : « من أذى شعرة منك فقد أذاني » ومن أذاني فقد أذى الله » ومن أذى الله قعليه لعنة الله , أ ه وهذا الحديث حمروي من طريق أبي خالد عن امامنا الخ في كتاب تنبيه الغافلين للحاكم أي سعيد المحسن بن كراعة + صاحب كتاب: الشفيكة + :وهئ مكل هذ شواء الى قوله : فقد أذاني , ثم قال : ومن أذى الله لعنه الله وملائكته ملأ السماء ؛ وملاً الارض ٠‏ وهى أيضا في كتاب درر السمطين للحافظ محمد بن يوسف الزرئدي الشافعي ٠‏ 5 . وام لع ا 0 م 6م قال ,. ده عيدية ؤم ل 3 : دعهما بتمتعان مىن. 2 | ع ممع هأ ]4 سيصيبهما بعدي أثرة7؟ ثم قال : يا أيها الناس إني خدّفت فيكم كتاب ما را الله ع وسني وعيرني أهل دي فالمضيع لكتاب | لله سد لسنبي والمضيم لسنبي كاطلضيم لعير بي » أما إن ذللتك لن يفرقا حبى لماه على الموض ) .
text_en:
The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, narrated to me while holding a hair of hers, saying: "Whoever harms a hair of yours has harmed me, and whoever harms me has harmed Allah, and whoever harms Allah, upon him is the curse of Allah." This hadith is narrated by Abu Khalid from our Imam al-Kha in the book Tanbih al-Ghafilin by al-Hakim, meaning Sa'id al-Muhsin ibn Karra'ah, the author of the book al-Shafiqah. And it is all like this, up to his saying: "has harmed me." Then he said: "And whoever harms Allah, Allah and His angels, filling the heavens and filling the earth, curse him." And it is also in the book Durar al-Simtayn by al-Hafiz Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Zarandi al-Shafi'i.

He said: "Let them enjoy themselves, for after me, they will be afflicted with favoritism." Then he said: "O people, I have left among you the Book of Allah and my Sunnah and my 'Itrah (family). So whoever neglects the Book of Allah has neglected my Sunnah, and whoever neglects my Sunnah has neglected my 'Itrah. Indeed, these two will not separate until they meet me at the Pond."

text_ar: ( حدثي ) زبك بن علي عن أديه عن جده عن علي ( رضي الله عنهم ا( | شور جلت أن ورسول الله ار تطوف 2 ل 3 وصاحب التعخل معنا » فإذا هو بمطهرة 7" معلقة على مخملة قال : فذةناول رس ول الله ار المطهرة وهو قائم فمجعل دشنها ف فيه 6 وهو الم 7 0) 0) تو التققام امطووق مكل :توكس :اليد التي ,وكويكنا نيا :لوقن الله أخرى بقتح الميم قال في شرح الشفاء لابن حنش في الديوأن يفتحها وهى أفصح ٠‏ وفى تفسير الثتثعليبى لقوله تعالى : « شهد الله أئه لا اله الا هى واللائكة :والى العلم “قائما بالقسط + له اله "الا هين العزوق السكيد ١‏ ع انم من بعالل قال قال دميو ل الله على الله هليه واليةتوسلكه. : « هن قرآها عند متامه خلق الله عن وجل منها سيعين ألف خلق يستغفرون له الى يوم القيامة 2 وروى الواحدي عن اين عمر عسن أبى واثل » عن عيد الله قال : قال رسيول الله صلى الله عليه وآله : دهن قال تعن قزاءكها ".وان كنيد .جما شنيف ١‏ التدا له بواستوديم” الله هذه الشهادة 2 وهي عنده وديعة إن الددن عند الله الاسلام الى قوله تعالى بغير حساب » » ثم قالها الاعمش مرارا وقال : قال رسول الله صلى الله علية وآله وسلم : « بجاء يصاحيها لبىوم القيامة فيقول الله عز وجل أن لعبدي هذأ عندي عهدا , وانا أحق من وفى بالعهد , ادخلوا عبد ي الجنة » قال الخووي : ولستحب لمن شرب قَاكّمأ أن يسنفيء لحديث صح ا الا ا د الكنوب هو اقيام قال لخ عنس تهبوب قاننا! فليسستفيء ‏ قالهن ا الك : لا كراهة في ذلك > لفحل النجي: حلي النها تنهار الم ويل 1ف روي سيم بهمه؟
text_en:
Zayd ibn Ali narrated from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with them all) that he said:

"I saw the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) circumambulating the Kaaba, and his companion was with us. Then, he came upon a water skin hanging on a camel saddle. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) took the water skin while standing and began to drink from it while standing."

(The narrator said: The word "مُطْهَرَة" (mutahharah) is with a dammah on the mim, and it is also said with a fathah on the mim. Ibn Hajar said in Sharh al-Shifa' that it is to open it, and it is more eloquent. In the tafsir of al-Tha'labi for His saying, the Exalted: "Allah bears witness that there is no god but He, and the angels, and those endowed with knowledge, standing firm in justice. There is no god but He, the All-Mighty, the All-Wise." (Surah Al-Imran, 3:18)

It is narrated from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Whoever recites it when he goes to sleep, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will create for him seventy thousand creations who will seek forgiveness for him until the Day of Resurrection."

Al-Wahidi narrated from Ibn Umar, from Abu Wa'il, from Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Whoever says it, and he is truthful, Allah will accept this testimony from him, and it is a trust with Him: 'Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam' until His saying 'without reckoning.'" Then al-A'mash repeated it several times and said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Its reciter will come on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will say: 'My servant has a covenant with Me, and I am the most deserving of fulfilling covenants. Enter My servant into Paradise.'"

Al-Khuwayy said: It is recommended for one who drinks while standing to vomit, due to a sound hadith. However, al-Khattabi said: There is no dislike in that, due to the action of the Prophet (peace be upon him) as narrated by al-Bukhari.

text_ar: ( حدثي ) زيد ,بن علي عن اوناع عله ع عل روعي عت قال : قال رسول الله ملام اول نا فاق الك اكلم خدّق” الدواة وهو قوله تعالى : ن” والقكم وما يسطرون ثم قال 7 لتسخط كل شيء هو كان إلى يوم القيامة. 0 خلق أو أجتل » أو رزّق : أو عتمسل” إلى ما هو صائر إليه من جالة أو لدان ب م صلق العقل فاسةنطقه افاجانة » فتمال : وعدزني وجحلالي ما ندلقت نولقةا هو أحب إلي ناث : بك أصول » وداث أعطى » أما وعزني لأكساناك 5 ألحيتة و تفداة فيمن أبغضت ذأ كل الناس عقلا” أندو فوم لله عز وجل وأطوعهم له وأنقص الناس” عقلا أخوفهم لاشيطان وأطوعهم له © . ( سول في ) زيك سن علي عن أديه عن جده عن عي رضي الله عنهم قال : أمرتي رسول الله لش بقتال الناكثين والقاسطين » والمارقين فما كنت لأترك شيئاً ما أمرني بها حبيبي رسول الله مَل
text_en:
Zayd ibn Ali, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "The first thing Allah created was the pen." Then He said to it: "Write!" So it wrote everything that was to be until the Day of Judgment. Then He created the inkwell, and that is His saying, the Exalted: "Nun. And the pen and what they inscribe." Then He said: "Everything that is created, or made, or provided, or done, until what it is destined for, whether it be from a state or a place, is written." Then He created the intellect and made it speak, and it spoke. So He said: "By My might and My majesty, I have not created a creation that is more beloved to Me than you. By you I take hold, and by you I give. By My might, I will make you dwell in the one I love, and I will make you a guide in the one I hate. The most intelligent of people are the most fearful of Allah, the Exalted and Majestic, and the most obedient to Him. And the least intelligent of people are the most fearful of Satan and the most obedient to him."

Zayd ibn Ali, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with them) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) commanded me to fight the oath-breakers, the unjust, and the renegades. So I would not leave anything that my beloved Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) commanded me to do.

text_en:
Zayd ibn Ali narrated from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Three men came to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him. The eldest of them asked: "What is your name?" He replied: "My name is Wa'il (or he said Afl)." He said: "Rather, your name is Muqbil." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, we are a household who practice medicine in our land, and Allah the Almighty has brought Islam, so we dislike to treat anything except with your permission." He, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed, Allah the Almighty has not sent down a disease except that He has sent down a cure for it, except for death and old age. So do not be shy to seek a cure for your diseases if you have not sought one." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the mu'dhat?" He said to them: "It is the thing that, when it is held in the stomach, kills, so it is not appropriate for you to treat it."

Zayd ibn Ali narrated from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "Do not kill snakes except for their evil ones." And he forbade killing snakes that are in houses. And the meaning of al-wa'il is the one who seeks refuge. And the saying of the poet: "He sought refuge with Allah from the one who sought refuge." He said: "He sought refuge."

text_en: Zayd ibn Ali, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with them, said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, who among people is most deserving of my good companionship and kindness?" He said: "Your mother." He said: "Then who?" He said: "Your mother." He said: "Then who?" He said: "Your mother." He said: "Then who?" He said: "Your father." He said: "Then who?" He said: "Your closest relatives, then those closest to them."

text_en: Zayd ibn Ali, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with them, said: A black woman used to pick up litter from the mosque of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him. The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, inquired about her, and they said: "She has passed away." Then he said: "Indeed, I saw for her what I saw. I saw her in Paradise, picking from its fruits." Then the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed, there are seven who are saved from the Fire: the drowned, the one who died in a fire, the one who died under a collapsed building, the one who died from a plague, the one who died from a stomach illness, the one who died while pregnant, and the one who died while defending his property. And the fasting ones, and the love of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, and the love of his Shia, and whoever recites three verses from the beginning of Surat al-An'am up to 'He knows what you earn' when he prays Fajr. And whoever remembers Allah Almighty with his tongue and heart, and those who seek forgiveness in the pre-dawn hours, and whoever does not envy people, and whoever honors his parents. And a man who leads people in prayer, and they are pleased with him. And a man who used to call the adhan every day and night. And a servant who fulfilled the right of Allah and the right of his family. And the one who fulfills the needs of people. And the Muhajirun. And a person who never walked between two people in dispute. And whoever never thought of evil. And the bearers of the Qur'an. And the people of piety. The word 'khalasi' (خلاسي) with a kasra means a child born to a white and a black parent, and a rooster between two hens (hindada) according to the dictionary. The intended meaning here is dark-skinned. This is the end of the hadith of Imam Zayd. And whoever causes harm in a mosque, that will be a sin upon him.

text_en:
Zayd ibn Ali, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with them all), said:

I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: "Whoever says: 'I seek forgiveness from Allah, the Almighty, Whom there is no god except Him, and I repent to Him,' Allah will forgive his sins, even if they were like the foam of the sea and the sand of Aalij."

(1) Al-Hawra: The intense whiteness of the white of the eye, and the intense blackness of the black of the eye. This is from the interpretation of rare words by Imam Zayd ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with him).
(2) Aalij: A place between Makkah and Madinah with much sand. Imam al-Murshid Billah (may Allah be pleased with him) said in his Al-Amali al-Khamisiyyah, verbatim: "Al-Sharif Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Hasani informed us, as I read to him, saying:"

text_en:
Zayd ibn Ali, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with them, said: The Messenger of Allah was given a gift of chickens. Some of them were cooked and some were roasted.

In al-Jami' al-Saghir by al-Suyuti, he said: Al-Daylami narrated from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said: "When you see a servant whom Allah has afflicted with poverty and illness, then Allah desires to purify him."

Zayd ibn Ali, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with them.

text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us from Imam Zayd ibn Ali from his father from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, taught Fatimah, may Allah be pleased with her, to say: "I seek forgiveness from Allah, besides whom there is no god, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting. And I seek His help, and I seek His protection, and I repent to Him." And he said: "Whoever says it once, Allah will forgive him and his parents. And whoever says it three times, Allah will forgive him and his parents and his relatives. And whoever says it four times, Allah will forgive him and his parents and his relatives, and the Ummah of Muhammad, peace be upon him."

And from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, that he said: "There will appear at the end of time a people who will appear pious and devout, but they will not forbid evil. And if salah and their evil deeds were to harm their wealth and their souls, they would abandon them. And the greatest jihad is enjoining good and forbidding evil. There, the wrath of Allah will descend upon them, and the righteous will perish among the wicked, and the weak will perish among the strong. Indeed, enjoining good and forbidding evil are among the duties, and they are a gift from the Most Gracious, and they make earnings lawful, and they build up the earth, and justice is achieved against enemies. So deny with your hearts, and forbid with your tongues, and strive with your swords, and do not fear the blame of the blamers."

Zayd ibn Ali narrated to me from his father from his grandfather from Ali, may Allah be pleased with them, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said: "My Ummah will not perish as long as they enjoin good, and forbid evil, and help the oppressed, and do not abandon the oppressor."

text_en:
Zayd ibn Ali said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed, those who love each other for the sake of Allah Almighty will be raised on a pillar of red ruby, with seventy thousand rooms within it. The people of Paradise will say: 'Let us go and look at those who love each other for the sake of Allah.' When they look upon them, their faces will shine upon the people of Paradise, just as the sun shines upon the people of the world. They will say: 'These are those who love each other for the sake of Allah.'"

He said: "Indeed, gambling is like eating the flesh of a pig, and gambling is like being smeared with the fat of a pig and its grease."

He, may Allah be pleased with him, said that he passed by a people who were playing with dice. He said: "This was the gambling of the Persians, and the arrows were the gambling of the Arabs."

text_en: Zayd ibn Ali, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed, I forbid you from singing and female singers."

text_en: Zayd ibn Ali narrated from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with them, that he said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said: "Ten things are from the people of Lot: chewing gum, letting the lower garment hang down, letting the lower garment drag, flying pigeons, throwing pebbles, making a noise, their gathering together for evil, and some of them playing with others."

text_en: Zayd ibn Ali, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) would not eat anything from the hot, the moist, or from the cold foods, nor from the fresh vegetables. And I saw the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) picking up the gourd from the plate. And I saw the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) eating fresh dates with bread.
